notes: Orange Tree (orangetree.in) is a Shopify store, fully reachable via direct HTTP (200s, no block); robots.txt has no Claude disallow. Discovery: enumerated the FULL collections.json catalog (300 collections, 2 pages) and checked main nav + the homepage mega-menu, which has a dedicated accordion section literally headed 'NEW ARRIVALS' containing: 'All New' -> /collections/new, and three site-defined tag-filtered children -- Furniture -> /collections/new/furniture, Lighting -> /collections/new/lighting, Decor -> /collections/new/decor (site UI spelled 'Décor'; rendered here as plain ASCII 'Decor'). This is a genuine site-exposed parent/children structure (New Arrivals > Furniture/Lighting/Decor New Arrivals), not an invented split -- preserved as a grouping row + 3 leaves. Counting method: /collections/new/<tag> is a Shopify collection+tag combo view with no dedicated products.json endpoint, so exact counts for the 3 children were computed by pulling the full /collections/new/products.json (377 unique ids, exact, exhaustive pagination) and filtering by each product's own 'tags' array for 'Furniture'/'lighting'/'decor' (216/119/20 respectively) -- cross-checked against raw /products/ link enumeration on the live paginated HTML of each /collections/new/<tag> page, which produced identical counts (216/119/20), so the tag-filter counts are verified exact, not estimated. 216+119+20=355 of 377 parent items carry one of the three tags; the remaining 22 have none of those tags (no further site-exposed sub-split exists for them, so not broken out). Cached collections.json products_count for the parent ('new' handle) is inflated (671 cached vs 377 exact), matching the known Shopify products_count-unreliable pattern on this store. Separately, a second, older-looking collection titled 'New Arrivals' (handle new-arrivals, 93 exact unique products) exists and IS listed in sitemap_collections_1.xml, but is NOT linked from main nav, the homepage 'NEW ARRIVALS' menu, banners, or any category page checked (furniture/lighting/decor/wall-decor) -- recorded separately below with a MANUAL REVIEW flag rather than silently merged into or dropped from the canonical nav-linked /collections/new structure; it is a distinct product set, not a simple alias (different handle, different count, not cross-verified against the 'new' set here).
